title: Radial EBUS guides 1.1mm cryo- versus forceps biopsy for peripheral pulmonary lesions- a randomized controlled trial
summary: The early detection and diagnosis of peripheral pulmonary lesions (PPL) represents the cornerstone in lung cancer mortality reduction. Surgical lung biopsy still represents the gold standard in diagnostic evaluation. Although technical advances allow minimal invasive techniques for clarification of most peripheral lesions, it still is associated with relevant side-effects such as pain and impaired mobility as well as potential peri- and postoperative complications. Thus, non-surgical biopsy techniques have gained attraction during the last decades.
conditions: Abnormal findings on diagnostic imaging of lung

interventions.name: Group A: after PPL localisation with rEBUS, patients receive 6x rEBUS-TBFB with the lock left in place
Group B: after PPL localisation with rEBUS, patients receive 6x rEBUS-TBCB with repositioning of the sheath after biopsie

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Patient with peripheral lung lesion(s) ≥1cm in size requiring evaluation
- Patient is a candidate for an elective rEBUS TBCB and rEBUS TBFB procedure in the opinion of the treating physician
Exclusion criteria:
-The patient is unable or unwilling to participate in this study
-The patient has participated in a research study on a drug or device that would interfere with this study within 30 days prior to enrollment in the study
-Female patients who are pregnant or breastfeeding
-The patient has contraindications to general anesthesia
